thread:
miriam: Heads-up — customer on Dedicated (VPC) reported intermittent 401s for API calls after they switched from NLB -> ALB last night. They say it only happens when traffic goes through our private gateway via istio-ingress. Repro steps in the ticket.
raj: Can you paste a minimal repro curl + headers we can run from inside the VPC? Also which Private gateway version?
miriam: Gateway: private-gw v1.18.2, istio 1.16, path: client -> ALB -> nginx-proxy (customer) -> istio-ingress -> private-gw -> inference. Customer sent this quick repro from inside their VPC:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://private-gw.customer.internal/v1/models/ggml:generate" -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

miriam: Sometimes it returns 200, sometimes 401. When 401 shows up their nginx access log still has the Authorization header, but private-gw logs show no Authorization or show a truncated header `Bearer abc...` (shorter than expected). They also see `x-forwarded-authorization` present intermittently.
raj: That smells like header fragmentation or a proxy rewriting step. Does the ALB/NGINX use HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 to the ingress? Any proxy protocol enabled on the NLB->ALB change?
alex: Customer confirmed ALB -> nginx uses HTTP/1.1, istio healthchecks are v2, no proxy-protocol on ALB. They did enable ALB sticky sessions for the upgrade window.
pat: Can you grab the private-gw debug logs around the 401s? Also try curl --http1.1 vs --http2 and see if it correlates.

miriam: Pasted the relevant private-gw snippet (redacted) from their instance where 401 happened:

```
[2026-03-12T23:05:12Z] req_id=xyz auth_header="" authorization_source="headers"
[2026-03-12T23:05:12Z] req_id=xyz auth_error="missing authorization header"
[2026-03-12T23:05:12Z] req_id=xyz client_ip=10.2.1.45 route=/v1/models/ggml:generate status=401

# 10s earlier from nginx access log on their side:
"GET /v1/models/ggml:generate HTTP/1.1" 200 - "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci...longtoken..."
```

raj: Interesting — nginx shows the full header but private-gw sees empty. Could be istio ext_authz filter stripping or an envoy header limit. Also ALB sometimes folds large headers into cookies or uses signed cookies; headers can get split if there are multiple commas/lengths.
alex: Two quick hypotheses:
  1) Istio/gateway is configured to strip `Authorization` by mistake in an ext-authz or policy (common with older ext_authz configs).
  2) Header gets moved to `x-forwarded-authorization` by some intermediate proxy and our private-gw isn't binding that mapping.

pat: Try this quick repro from inside their VPC to see header propagation in plain text (we can run it via their jump host):

```
# run on jump host (tcpdump) to see if auth header leaves nginx
sudo tcpdump -A -s0 -i eth0 'tcp and port 443' | grep -i "Authorization"
```

miriam: Support ran that. They observed Authorization on traffic to ALB -> nginx, but between istio-ingress and private-gw tcpdump shows `Authorization` missing and `x-forwarded-authorization` present with the same token in some samples.
raj: If an Envoy filter rewrites Authorization -> x-forwarded-authorization for auditing, but our private-gw only reads `Authorization`, that explains 401s. We should handle both.

alex: Quick workaround we can ask customer to apply on their istio side (until we patch): add an Envoy header_to_metadata + request_header_transform to copy `x-forwarded-authorization` back to `authorization` before routing to private-gw. Example envoy config snippet they can try:

```
# Envoy Lua or header rewrite
filter_chains:
  - filters:
      - name: envoy.filters.http.lua
        typed_config:
          "inline_code": "function envoy_on_request(request_handle) local h = request_handle:headers(); if h:get('x-forwarded-authorization') and not h:get('authorization') then h:add('authorization', h:get('x-forwarded-authorization')) end end"
```

miriam: I shared that snippet. Customer applied and reported immediate drop in 401s over the next 15 minutes :thumbsup: . They can't keep that long-term w/o approval from infra but it proves the mapping is the culprit.
pat: Let's create an internal ticket to update private-gw to accept `x-forwarded-authorization` as fallback (config toggle), and add tracing for header presence. Also add an entry to the runbook: "When 401s after LB changes -> check for auth header being moved to x-forwarded-authorization or cookies."
raj: Agreed. Also ask eng-infra to audit ext_authz policies in istio-ingress for any rules that set `strip_authorization_header: true` (we've seen that in a couple onboarding scripts).

sre-bot: Created issue INFRA-7421: "private-gw: fallback to x-forwarded-authorization and improve header tracing" assigned to eng-runtime. Link: https://internal.redwood/INFRA-7421

miriam: Filed support case with the customer explaining temporary workaround and ETA for a more permanent fix. Marking as escalated -> eng-runtime. Closing thread here but leaving logs attached to INFRA-7421.
alex: Nice triage. Also note: if ALB->proxy switches to http2, header compression/HPACK can sometimes interact poorly with intermediate proxies. If it resurfaces, we'll capture pcap and full envoy traces.

pat: TL;DR: root cause = intermediate proxy (istio/envoy) moving Authorization -> x-forwarded-authorization during ALB migration. Workaround = rewrite/copy header back. Long-term = make private-gw tolerant and add runbook check.
